mainTopic: Whether מעשר שני is a דבר שיש לו מתירין under חזקיה, tested against a ברייתא that says it is cancelled in a majority
overview: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה from ביכורים that lists rules for תרומה and ביכורים that do not apply to מעשר. It reads 'not so with מעשר' to mean that מעשר שני is cancelled in a simple majority. That creates a problem for חזקיה: if even tiny amounts of מעשר שני can always be redeemed, it is a דבר שיש לו מתירין and should never be cancelled. After some back-and-forth over how to read the משנה, a ברייתא says outright that מעשר שני is cancelled in a majority in two cases. The first case is מעשר worth less than a פרוטה, and the second is מעשר that entered ירושלים and left. For the first case, the גמרא explains that the owner has no first coins. It then rejects every other way to redeem the half-פרוטה: joining it with other מעשר, using דמאי, using two פרוטות, or using an איסר. For the second case, the גמרא asks why he can't just bring it back, and answers that it became טמא. It then asks why he can't redeem it, citing רבי אלעזר, and that quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the משנה: rules for תרומה and ביכורים that do not apply to מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more laws shared by תרומה and ביכורים and ends by saying these do not apply to מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are forbidden to non-כהנים, they belong to the כהן as his property, they are only cancelled in a mixture of 101, they require hand-washing, and someone who was טמא must wait for sunset. These apply to תרומה and ביכורים, but not to מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה that it started just before this. It is setting up a source that it will use in the next step to challenge חזקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list compares תרומה and ביכורים, which share many laws. The last line, 'which is not so with מעשר,' is the key phrase. The rest of the discussion depends on what that line means for mixtures.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן's own property, which he can sell or use like money
Cancelled in a mixture of 1 part in 101
Waiting for sunset after immersing in a מקוה
Tithe; here it means מעשר שני

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that 'עולים באחד ומאה' is about mixtures. That is exactly why the phrase 'not so with מעשר' becomes a question about how מעשר gets cancelled in a mixture.

phrases.english: And they are forbidden to non-priests,
phrases.notes: This picks up in the middle of a משנה (ביכורים 2:1) that the גמרא began quoting just before.

phrases.english: and they are the property of the priest,
and they are cancelled in one and a hundred,
phrases.notes: Literally 'they go up in 101.' One part gets cancelled only when there are 100 parts of regular food mixed in.

phrases.english: and they require washing of the hands
and sunset.
These apply to terumah and first fruits,
which is not so with tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Several laws, including being cancelled only in 101, apply to תרומה and ביכורים but not to מעשר.

steps.title: Reading the משנה: מעשר is cancelled in a simple majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that 'not so with מעשר' means מעשר שני does not need 101 and is cancelled in a simple majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'not so with מעשר' mean? Doesn't it imply that מעשר is cancelled in a simple majority?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the last line of the משנה. This sets up the challenge against חזקיה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה needs 1 in 101 to be cancelled. If מעשר is 'not like that,' the natural reading is that מעשר is easier and is cancelled in a regular majority (ביטול ברוב).

phrases.english: What does "which is not so with tithe" mean?
Isn't it implied that tithe
is cancelled in a majority?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the last line of the משנה
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר שני is cancelled in a simple majority
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast in the משנה: תרומה needs 101, but 'not so with מעשר'

steps.title: Challenge to חזקיה: a דבר שיש לו מתירין is never cancelled
steps.stepSummary: If חזקיה is right that tiny amounts of מעשר שני can always be redeemed, then מעשר is a דבר שיש לו מתירין and should never be cancelled, which goes against the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If חזקיה is right, מעשר is something that has a way to become permitted, and anything like that is not cancelled even in a thousand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the inference from the משנה to attack חזקיה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that something which can become permitted another way (דבר שיש לו מתירין) is never cancelled in a mixture. If חזקיה says even less than a פרוטה of מעשר שני can be redeemed, then מעשר always has a way out. So it should never be cancelled, but the משנה implies it is cancelled in a majority.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so (introduces a challenge to someone's view)
Something that has a way to become permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of דבר שיש לו מתירין is a major principle in the laws of mixtures. Here it is the engine of the whole challenge.

phrases.english: And if Chizkiyah's view is correct,
phrases.notes: חזקיה said earlier that even מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה can be redeemed, using the earlier coins.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה לֵיהּ דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין.
phrases.english: it is an item that has a way to become permitted.
And any item that has a way to become permitted
is not cancelled even in a thousand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 2 to attack חזקיה
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's view that מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה can be redeemed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it can always be redeemed, it is a דבר שיש לו מתירין and should never be cancelled. But the משנה implies it is cancelled in a majority.

steps.title: Maybe מעשר is never cancelled at all
steps.stepSummary: The inference is pushed back: 'not so with מעשר' might mean מעשר is not cancelled at all, not that it is cancelled more easily.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know 'not so with מעשר' means it is cancelled in a majority? Maybe it isn't cancelled at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the reading from step 2. If this works, the challenge to חזקיה falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not like תרומה' could go in either direction. It could be easier (a majority is enough) or stricter (it is never cancelled). If it is stricter, that fits חזקיה perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you know?

phrases.english: And from where do you know that "which is not so with tithe"
means it is cancelled in a majority?
Perhaps it is not cancelled at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference that the challenge was built on
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of 'not so with מעשר' from step 2
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase could mean מעשר is stricter (never cancelled), not more lenient

steps.title: The משנה lists only stringencies of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The pushback is answered: the משנה lists only the strict laws of תרומה, so 'not so with מעשר' must mean מעשר is more lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can't say that. Regarding תרומה, the משנה teaches its stringencies, not its leniencies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the original reading from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the list is all about how strict תרומה is, then 'not so with מעשר' means מעשר is less strict. So 1-in-101 is a strict rule for תרומה, and מעשר is cancelled with less, in a simple majority.

phrases.english: You cannot say so,
because regarding terumah
it teaches the stringencies of terumah,
it does not teach the leniencies of terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the nature of the משנה's list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not so with מעשר' might mean מעשר is stricter
steps.terutzMaskana: The list contains only stringencies of תרומה, so מעשר must be more lenient

steps.title: But the משנה lists a leniency: they are the כהן's property
steps.stepSummary: The defense is challenged: 'they are the property of the כהן' is a leniency, so the משנה does not list only stringencies.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה does teach 'and they are the property of the כהן'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from step 5 by pointing to an item in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being the כהן's own property, which he can sell or use, is a good thing, not a strict rule. So the list mixes strict and lenient laws, and the reading 'מעשר is never cancelled' is possible again.

phrases.english: But it does teach:
"and they are the property of the priest"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא תָנֵי וְהֵן נִכְסֵי כֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה lists only stringencies of תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה includes 'they are the property of the כהן,' which is a leniency

steps.title: A ברייתא says plainly: מעשר שני is cancelled in a majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the reading from the משנה and brings a ברייתא that says outright that מעשר שני is cancelled in a majority, in specific cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, because a ברייתא says it openly: מעשר שני is cancelled in a majority. Which מעשר שני did they mean? מעשר worth less than a פרוטה, and מעשר that entered ירושלים and then left.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of arguing about the משנה, the גמרא proves from a clear ברייתא that מעשר שני can be cancelled in a majority. This sets up the challenge to חזקיה again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no doubt that מעשר שני is sometimes cancelled in a majority. The ברייתא limits this to two cases: מעשר worth less than a פרוטה, and מעשר that went into ירושלים and came out. The next step tests the less-than-a-פרוטה case against חזקיה; the second case is taken up in steps 18-21.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught openly in a ברייתא
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest coin value

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא settles it: מעשר שני is cancelled in a simple majority in two cases: when it is worth less than a פרוטה, and when it entered ירושלים and left.

phrases.english: Do not even think that,
because it is taught openly:
Second tithe is cancelled in a majority.
And about which second tithe did they say this?
About tithe that is not worth a peruta,
and that entered Jerusalem and left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the debate over the משנה by bringing a clear ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר שני is cancelled in a majority

steps.title: Renewed challenge: why not redeem it on the first coins like חזקיה?
steps.stepSummary: If חזקיה is right, the מעשר in the ברייתא could be redeemed on the first coins, so it is a דבר שיש לו מתירין and should not be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: If חזקיה is right, let him do what חזקיה says and redeem it on the first coins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the challenge to חזקיה, now using the ברייתא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה lets a person redeem even less than a פרוטה by adding it to coins he already used for an earlier redemption. If that is possible here, this מעשר has a way to become permitted. Then the ברייתא should not say it is cancelled in a majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him redeem it (transfer its holiness)
The first coins, already used for an earlier redemption

phrases.english: And if Chizkiyah's view is correct,
let him act according to Chizkiyah,
and redeem it on the first coins!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from step 7 to the challenge of step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under חזקיה the מעשר could be redeemed on the first coins, so it is a דבר שיש לו מתירין and could not be cancelled, which contradicts the ברייתא

steps.title: The case is where he never redeemed before
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about someone who never did an earlier redemption, so he has no first coins to use.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he did not redeem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and saves חזקיה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה's method only works if there are 'first coins' from an earlier redemption. In the ברייתא's case there are none, so this מעשר has no way to become permitted, and it can be cancelled in a majority.
steps.whatToRemember: For now, חזקיה's view survives: the ברייתא is about someone with no earlier redemption coins. The next steps test whether he has any other way to redeem it.

phrases.english: Where he did not redeem.
phrases.notes: He never redeemed any מעשר שני before, so there are no 'first coins' to add this to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's מעשר could always be redeemed on first coins
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about someone who has no first coins, so the מעשר can be cancelled in a majority

steps.title: Why not join it with other מעשר he owns?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests he bring another half-פרוטה of מעשר שני that he owns and join it to the mixed half-פרוטה, making it redeemable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him bring other מעשר that he has, and join them together!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 9. Even without first coins, he could still find a way to redeem the mixed מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mixed-in מעשר is worth too little to redeem alone. If he adds another half-פרוטה of מעשר, the total reaches a full פרוטה and can be redeemed. That would make it a דבר שיש לו מתירין again, and then it should not be cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe; produce eaten in ירושלים or redeemed onto coins
Joining two small amounts into one amount that counts
Something that will become permitted in another way, so it is not cancelled in a majority

phrases.english: But let him bring other tithe produce that he has
and join them together!
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the one in square brackets. Both mean 'join'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 9's claim that this person has no way to redeem the מעשר
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא's case has no permitting factor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Joining with other מעשר would bring it to a full פרוטה and make redemption possible

steps.title: Torah-level and rabbinic-level מעשר do not join
steps.stepSummary: The other מעשר is מעשר by Torah law, but the mixed half-פרוטה is only מעשר by rabbinic law, and the two kinds cannot join.
steps.simpleTranslation: Torah-level and rabbinic-level do not join.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the two pieces of מעשר are different levels, so they cannot be added together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law the mixed half-פרוטה was already cancelled in the majority. It keeps a holy status only because of the rabbinic rule about דבר שיש לו מתירין. The new half-פרוטה is fully Torah-level מעשר, so the two are not the same kind and cannot add up to a פרוטה.

phrases.english: Torah-level and rabbinic-level do not join.
phrases.notes: The mixed-in half is only rabbinic, since by Torah law it was already cancelled in the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Legal principle blocks the suggested method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any two half-פרוטות of מעשר can be added together
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah-level and rabbinic-level מעשר cannot join, so this method fails

steps.title: Why not join it with מעשר from דמאי?
steps.stepSummary: Then let him join it with a half-פרוטה of מעשר taken from דמאי, which is also only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him bring מעשר from דמאי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again. It suggests using rabbinic-level מעשר, so both pieces are the same level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 blocked joining because the levels were different. מעשר from דמאי is only rabbinic, just like the mixed half-פרוטה. So the two should be able to join.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce bought from an unlearned person that may not have been tithed; tithing it is only rabbinic

phrases.english: But let him bring tithe from doubtfully tithed produce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works around the problem raised in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא's case has no permitting factor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two rabbinic-level pieces should join, so redemption is possible

steps.title: He might end up using definite untithed produce
steps.stepSummary: This is not allowed, because he might come to use מעשר from produce that was definitely untithed, which is Torah-level.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will come to bring from definite produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן would not allow this method because it could lead to a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People handle דמאי almost the same way as definitely untithed produce. If this method were allowed, he could mix them up and use Torah-level מעשר. That would be a Torah-level piece joining a rabbinic one, which does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Definite; here, produce that was surely not tithed

phrases.english: Perhaps he will come to bring from definitely untithed produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using דמאי מעשר is a clean solution
steps.terutzMaskana: It is not allowed up front, because he may mistakenly use Torah-level מעשר

steps.title: Why not redeem a פרוטה and a half on two פרוטות?
steps.stepSummary: Let him redeem a פרוטה and a half of מעשר onto two פרוטות. That leaves half a פרוטה of 'room', which he can use to redeem the mixed half-פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him bring two פרוטות, redeem a פרוטה and a half of מעשר on them, and then redeem this mixed half on that extra space.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a third method, this time using coins instead of extra produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פרוטות can hold two פרוטות' worth of holiness. If he first redeems only a פרוטה and a half, there seems to be half a פרוטה of space left. He could then redeem the small mixed amount onto that space, so the mixed מעשר would have a way to be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The smallest coin; the least amount that can be redeemed
Redeeming; moving the holiness from produce onto coins

phrases.english: But let him bring two perutot,
and redeem upon them tithe worth one and a half perutot,
and redeem this one upon that extra one.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the mixed half-פרוטה; 'that extra one' is the leftover half-פרוטה of space on the coins.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנַיְתֵי שְׁתֵּי פְרוּטוֹת, וּנְחַלֵּל עֲלַיְיהוּ מַעֲשֵׂר בִּפְרוּטָה וּמֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new method after steps 10–13 failed
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא's case has no permitting factor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leftover space on two פרוטות would let him redeem the mixed half-פרוטה

steps.title: The extra half-פרוטה never takes hold on the coins
steps.stepSummary: The holiness does not spread over both coins. One פרוטה of holiness goes onto one coin, and the extra half does not take hold at all. So we are back to Torah-level and rabbinic-level halves, which do not join.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think a פרוטה and a half takes hold on two פרוטות? No. A פרוטה takes hold on a פרוטה, and the half-פרוטה does not take hold. So it is again Torah-level and rabbinic-level, and those do not join.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the coin plan by showing the way the holiness actually moves onto the coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redemption works in whole פרוטות. Only one full פרוטה of the produce moves onto one coin. The leftover half-פרוטה of produce stays holy, because less than a פרוטה cannot be redeemed. He is left with a Torah-level half and a rabbinic-level half again, and step 11 already said those cannot join.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think? (a set phrase that brings up an assumption in order to reject it)
Takes hold; the holiness moves onto the coin
It goes back to being; we are back to the same problem

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture the holiness as spreading evenly over both coins. It goes on in whole-פרוטה units, so the extra half of produce stays unredeemed. No 'empty half-coin' is left over.

phrases.aramaic: מִי סָבְרַתְּ: פְּרוּטָה וּמֶחֱצָה תָּפְסָה שְׁתֵּי פְרוּטוֹת?
phrases.english: Do you think a peruta and a half takes hold on two perutot?
No. A peruta takes hold on a peruta,
and the half peruta does not take hold.
phrases.notes: The half-פרוטה of produce stays holy, because it is too small to move onto a coin.

phrases.english: So it goes back to being Torah-level and rabbinic-level.
And Torah-level and rabbinic-level do not join.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ: פְּרוּטָה וּמֶחֱצָה תָּפְסָה שְׁתֵּי פְרוּטוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 14 and brings it back to the rule of step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The two-פרוטות method as a whole
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes the holiness spreads over both coins, but only whole פרוטות take hold

steps.title: Why not redeem on an איסר?
steps.stepSummary: Let him use an איסר, a larger coin worth eight פרוטות, so the leftover space could hold the mixed half-פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him bring an איסר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a fourth method: use one bigger coin instead of small פרוטות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסר is one coin worth eight פרוטות. It is not split into separate פרוטה coins, so the holiness could spread over it without needing whole-פרוטה units. That would leave real room for the mixed half-פרוטה.

phrases.english: But let him bring an issar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works around the whole-פרוטה problem of step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא's case has no permitting factor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single large coin avoids the problem of separate פרוטות

steps.title: He might end up using פרוטות
steps.stepSummary: This is not allowed, because he might come to use separate פרוטות instead, and then the plan would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will come to bring פרוטות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last suggestion with the same kind of worry used for דמאי. This closes the discussion of the less-than-a-פרוטה case; the next step turns to the ברייתא's second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן allowed the איסר method, people might use small פרוטות instead. As step 15 showed, with פרוטות the half never takes hold. So no method is allowed, the mixed מעשר has no way to be permitted, and the ברייתא can say it is cancelled in a majority.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring; here, to end up using

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the four ways to redeem the mixed half-פרוטה fails. Torah-level and rabbinic-level מעשר cannot join, and the רבנן blocked the other methods so people would not slip into mistakes. So the ברייתא's מעשר is not a דבר שיש לו מתירין, and it is cancelled in a majority even according to חזקיה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defends the ברייתא as a proof that מעשר שני can be cancelled in a majority. It shows that a theoretical way to permit something does not count if the רבנן did not allow it.

phrases.english: Perhaps he will come to bring perutot.
phrases.notes: With separate פרוטות the extra half never takes hold, as the גמרא just showed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 and closes the series of suggestions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An איסר solves the whole-פרוטה problem
steps.terutzMaskana: It is not allowed up front, because he may use פרוטות, where the plan fails

steps.title: Another case in the ברייתא: produce that entered ירושלים and left
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the ברייתא: מעשר שני that was brought into ירושלים and then taken back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא also lists: מעשר שני that entered ירושלים and then went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next case from the ברייתא it has been discussing. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about the half-פרוטה of mixed produce. Now the focus moves to the ברייתא's second case: מעשר שני that was inside ירושלים and then left. The גמרא is about to ask why this case is not a דבר שיש לו מתירין.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe: produce that must be eaten in ירושלים, or redeemed for money that is then brought there

phrases.english: And [second tithe] that entered Jerusalem and went out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the half-פרוטה discussion (steps 14-17) to the next case listed in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא includes מעשר שני that entered ירושלים and left among its special cases.

steps.title: Why not just bring it back into ירושלים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this case needs a special rule. The owner could simply carry the produce back into ירושלים and eat it there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why should it be cancelled? Let him bring it back into ירושלים, and then it can be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ruling on this case. If the owner can just take the produce back into ירושלים and eat it there, it has a way to become permitted, so it should not be cancelled in a majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני is meant to be eaten in ירושלים. If it only stepped outside, nothing seems to stop him from returning it and eating it. That makes it a דבר שיש לו מתירין, which should not be cancelled even in a thousand, so the ברייתא's ruling that it is cancelled in a majority is hard to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: And why? A question that challenges a ruling

phrases.english: But why? Let him go back and bring it in!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case quoted in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's listing of 'entered ירושלים and left' as a special case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He can bring the produce back into ירושלים and eat it. So it has a way to become permitted (דבר שיש לו מתירין) and should not be cancelled in a majority.

steps.title: The produce became טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is one where the produce became טמא, so bringing it back would not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about produce that became impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the case. The produce became טמא, so it can't simply be brought back and eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני that is טמא may not be eaten, even in ירושלים. So returning it is not a way to make it permitted. Without that route it is not a דבר שיש לו מתירין, and it can be cancelled in a majority.

phrases.english: Where it became impure.
phrases.notes: Impure מעשר שני can't be eaten, so bringing it back to ירושלים wouldn't help.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The produce is still fit to eat, so it could just be brought back.
steps.terutzMaskana: The produce became טמא, so it can no longer be eaten even in ירושלים.

steps.title: Then why not redeem it, as רבי אלעזר teaches?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if it is טמא, he should just redeem it. It begins quoting רבי אלעזר, who brings a source that טמא מעשר שני may be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him redeem it! As רבי אלעזר said: from where do we know that מעשר שני that became impure may be redeemed...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the produce is טמא, he can simply redeem it, and it begins quoting רבי אלעזר as support. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 20 showed that returning the produce is useless. But טמא מעשר שני has another route: redeem it onto money. That would make it a דבר שיש לו מתירין again, and then it should not be cancelled in a majority.

keyTerms.meaning: From where [do we know]? Asks for a source

steps.confusionAlert: Normally מעשר שני that has entered ירושלים can no longer be redeemed. The גמרא is pointing out that טמא produce is treated differently and may be redeemed.

phrases.english: But let him redeem it!
As Rabbi Elazar said:
From where do we know, regarding second tithe that became impure,
that we redeem it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20. Even if it is טמא, there is a simple solution.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the produce became טמא (step 20)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: טמא מעשר שני may be redeemed, according to רבי אלעזר. So it still has a way to become permitted, and it should not be cancelled in a majority.
